title: Punctual purity and regular closed pairs: two of three
statement:
For a prime $\ell$ and $A=\mathbf F_\ell$, use ordinary small-etale derived categories and Tate twists [def-weil-pbc-derived-categories, def-asd-finite-etale-tate-twist]. If $W$ is a regular Noetherian scheme with $\ell$ invertible [def-weil-regular-scheme], say that $W$ is punctually pure at $w\in W$ when, for $W_w=\operatorname{Spec}\mathcal O_{W,w}$, $d_w=\dim\mathcal O_{W,w}$ and its closed-point inclusion $j_w:\operatorname{Spec}\kappa(w)\hookrightarrow W_w$, the Kummer fundamental-class map
$$A_{\kappa(w)}\longrightarrow j_w^!A_{W_w}(d_w)[2d_w]$$
of [lem-per-regular-immersion-class-calculus] is an isomorphism. Say that $W$ is punctually pure when this holds at every point. Local rings and residue fields are as in [def-weil-residue-field], affine spectra as in [def-weil-affine-spectrum], and dimension as in [def-weil-pbc-krull-dimension-ring].

Let $i:Z\hookrightarrow X$ be a closed immersion between regular Noetherian schemes on which $\ell$ is invertible, locally of constant codimension $c$ [def-weil-closed-immersion]. Among the following conditions, any two imply the third:
(a) the supported Kummer map $A_Z\to i^!A_X(c)[2c]$ is an isomorphism;
(b) $Z$ is punctually pure;
(c) $X$ is punctually pure at every point of $i(Z)$.
The statement applies also to localizations of the pair.

source.place: Expose XVI, Definitions 3.1.4 and 3.2.1--3.2.2, Proposition 3.2.3 and proof, printed pp.243--244 (pointwise Gysin composition and cone supported at a closed point).

proof.text: Work on a component where the codimension is $c$. For $z\in Z$, set $x=i(z)$, $R=\mathcal O_{X,x}$, $D=\dim R$ and $B=\mathcal O_{Z,z}=R/I$. These are regular local rings and $I$ is proper. By the codimension hypothesis, read through the stalkwise definition [def-per-stalk-regular-closed-immersion], $I$ is generated by an $R$-regular sequence $f_1,\ldots,f_c$. A regular system of parameters of $R$ is an $R$-regular sequence of length $D$ by the parameter-sequence theorem, so $R$ is Cohen--Macaulay in the sense of [lem-weil-pbc-cm-local-quotient-nonzerodivisor-cm]. Applying that lemma $c$ times, to $R/(f_1,\ldots,f_{k-1})$ and its nonzerodivisor $f_k$ for $k=1,\ldots,c$, gives $\dim B=D-c$. The regular-quotient kernel theorem supplies parameters $t_1,\ldots,t_D$ of $R$ and an integer $c'$ with $I=(t_1,\ldots,t_{c'})$; the parameter-sequence theorem says this is a regular sequence and $\dim B=D-c'$. Hence $c'=c$. In particular $D=\dim B+c$, the closed-point immersions of both local schemes are regular, and their composite is the closed-point immersion into $\operatorname{Spec}R$. The quotient map has the same residue field on both sides. Regularity at any further localization follows from the local-ring definition of regularity. Thus all the regular-immersion classes used below are defined, including when $c=0$.

source.place: Expose XVI, Proposition 3.2.3, local diagram; local algebra: Stacks algebra.tex Tags 00NR (lemma-regular-quotient-regular) and 00NQ (lemma-regular-ring-CM)

proof.text:
Write $V=\operatorname{Spec}B$, $T=\operatorname{Spec}R$, $i':V\hookrightarrow T$, and $a:s=\operatorname{Spec}\kappa(z)\hookrightarrow V$. Put $d=\dim B$ and $b=i'a$. At level $n=1$, let $g=\eta_{i'}:A_V\to i'^!A_T(c)[2c]$. Localization compatibility of the class family identifies this map with the restriction of the original supported Kummer map. Gysin composition, with the twist-shifts combined, gives
$$\eta_b=a^!(g)(d)[2d]\circ\eta_a,$$
where $\eta_a:A_s\to a^!A_V(d)[2d]$ and $\eta_b:A_s\to b^!A_T(d+c)[2(d+c)]$. Exceptional transitivity in that composition formula identifies the target of $a^!(g)(d)[2d]$ with the target of $\eta_b$. By the definition of punctual purity, (b) asserts that every $\eta_a$ is invertible and (c) asserts that every $\eta_b$ is invertible. The localization comparison invoked here is only the published comparison for these constant-coefficient supported classes, not a base-change claim for arbitrary inputs.

source.place: Expose XVI, Proposition 3.2.3 and its proof, printed p.244

proof.text: Assume (a). Then its localized map $g$ is invertible, and hence $a^!(g)(d)[2d]$ is invertible, since every functor preserves inverses. In the identity of step 2, if $\eta_a$ is invertible then $\eta_b$ is invertible. Conversely, if $\eta_b$ is invertible then $\eta_a=(a^!(g)(d)[2d])^{-1}\circ\eta_b$ is invertible. Applying this at every $z$ proves (a)+(b)$\Rightarrow$(c) and (a)+(c)$\Rightarrow$(b).

source.place: Expose XVI, Proposition 3.2.3 and its proof, printed p.244

proof.text:
Now assume (b) and (c). In the same identity both $\eta_a$ and $\eta_b$ are invertible, so
$$a^!(g)(d)[2d]=\eta_b\circ\eta_a^{-1}$$
is invertible for every local pair. The finite-twist lemma gives a locally free rank-one Tate line and its dual negative twist. Their evaluation is an isomorphism, since after a trivializing etale cover it is the identity on $A$. Thus the twist-shift is an equivalence, with inverse $(-d)[-2d]$. Consequently $a^!g$ is invertible. This conclusion alone concerns supported restriction, not ordinary restriction to $s$; the next steps supply the missing passage.

source.place: Expose XVI, Proposition 3.2.3 and its proof, printed p.244

proof.text: Prove that $g$ is invertible for every such local pair by strong induction on the finite integer $d=\dim B$. Let $C$ be a cone of $g$ in $D^+(V_{\mathrm{et}},A)$ and let $u:V\setminus\{z\}\hookrightarrow V$. If $q\ne z$ is a point of $V$, then $\dim B_q<d$: a chain of primes ending in $q$ extends strictly by the maximal ideal of $B$. The localized pair at $q$ again satisfies (b) and (c), since its point local rings are the same as the original point local rings. The induction hypothesis therefore makes its supported Kummer map invertible. Localization compatibility of the class family identifies it with the restriction of $g$ at $q$. Exact inverse image applied termwise preserves cone triangles, so the restriction of $C$ to this localization is zero. Every geometric stalk of $\mathcal H^r(u^*C)$ is consequently zero: compute it in the localization at its underlying $q$, using exactness of geometric stalks. Stalk conservativity applied to each cohomology sheaf gives $u^*C=0$. If $d=0$, there is no $q\ne z$, since any such prime would give a chain of positive length; the same vanishing holds on the empty complement. This starts the induction without assuming purity in dimension zero.

source.place: Expose XVI, Proposition 3.2.3 and its proof, printed p.244

proof.text: The exceptional functors in the class family are the right adjoints of [thm-amb-etale-exceptional-adjoint] for the compactification of [def-amb-etale-compact-support] with open part the identity and proper part the closed immersion itself, which is proper by [lem-weil-pbc-closed-immersion-proper]. Extension by zero along the identity is the identity, and the derived direct image of a closed immersion is its exact termwise direct image, as recorded in [def-per-closed-support-plus-adjunction]; so for $a$ this right adjoint is a right adjoint of $a_*$. By uniqueness of right adjoints it is canonically isomorphic to the right adjoint $Ra^!$ of [lem-exc-closed-ambient], and, on bounded-below objects, to the closed-support functor $a^!$ of [def-per-closed-support-plus-adjunction], which is stated there to be the bounded-below closed-support adjoint of that lemma; likewise for $i'$ and $b$. These identifications are compatible with the adjunction transposes, so the maps $\eta_a$ and $\eta_b$ of step 2 are those of [def-per-punctual-purity], the map $a^!g$ of step 4 is the map below, and the object $a^!C$ below is the object $Ra^!C$ of step 7. The functor $a^!$ is the derived closed-support functor specified by the closed-support adjunction. Right derived additive functors carry distinguished triangles to distinguished triangles. Applying it to the cone triangle for $g$, and using step 4, gives a distinguished triangle whose first arrow $a^!g$ is invertible and whose third object is $a^!C$. The cohomology long exact sequence then gives $\mathcal H^r(a^!C)=0$ for every $r$, so $a^!C=0$. All inputs are bounded below; the same derived support functor is viewed in the ordinary derived category, and no constructibility or dualizing-complex hypothesis is used.

source.place: Expose XVI, Proposition 3.2.3 and its proof, printed p.244

proof.text:
Apply the ordinary etale closed-support triangle to $a:s\hookrightarrow V$ and $C$:
$$a_*a^!C\longrightarrow C\longrightarrow Ru_*u^*C\longrightarrow(a_*a^!C)[1].$$
Steps 5 and 6 make its outer terms zero. Its cohomology long exact sequence therefore gives $C=0$, and the cone triangle gives that $g$ is invertible. This completes the induction. For the original map on $Z$, take its cone $C_Z$. The comparison of localized constant-coefficient Kummer maps now gives $(C_Z)|_{\operatorname{Spec}\mathcal O_{Z,z}}=0$ for every $z$. Exact geometric stalks and their conservativity, degree by degree, imply $C_Z=0$. Thus the original map is invertible, proving (b)+(c)$\Rightarrow$(a). Empty $Z$ is included: there are no stalks to test. The same argument starts with any localized pair; its regular local rings, residue fields, classes and codimensions are precisely those used above. This proves the final localization assertion.

tool_uses.why: Generic ordinary etale finite Tate-line and dual-line comparison makes the twist cancellable; only ell-invertible finite coefficients are used.
Generic regular-local quotient algebra establishes that the local closed pair is a regular immersion; this unit has no local algebra replacement.

Exact ordinary etale inverse image is the generic restriction tool for localized cone triangles.
Generic conservativity of ordinary etale geometric stalks detects zero cohomology sheaves; no duality detection is used.
Generic derived-functor exactness applied to the actual closed-support right derived functor; no Picard geometry or duality is imported.
Generic ordinary etale closed-support triangle kills the cone supported at the closed point; the unit provides no replacement.
Generic Cohen-Macaulay dimension drop identifies the given codimension with the length from the regular-quotient kernel theorem (reviewer repair, step 1).
Identifies the class family's exceptional right adjoint, for a closed immersion, with the closed-support adjoint used in steps 6-7 (reviewer repair).
Ordinary unbounded closed-support right adjoint, the functor of the support triangle of step 7 (reviewer repair).
